guide.title: Valla's Overview
guide.text:
Valla is a highly versatile and flexible ranged damage dealer. Her strong
points are her exceptional single-target damage and on-demand area of effect
burst damage. However, her relative fragility makes her a high priority target
for the enemy.

guide.title: Valla's Strengths and Weaknesses
guide.text:
Strengths
Very high single-target and area of effect damage
Good waveclear
Good poke
Strong in all phases of the game
Flexible Talents that allow her to adapt to many different situations
Weaknesses
Dependent on good positioning
Low base Health
Vulnerable to crowd control

guide.title: Valla's Synergies and Counters
guide.text:
Valla synergizes with
Valla is at her best when something stands between her and her enemies.
Large, Healthy Tanks are particularly desirable as they draw attention
away from Valla, and often provide their own form of crowd control for
potential follow-ups. Otherwise, anything that can protect Valla is also
desirable. Shielding effects are particularly impactful due to her limited
Health pool.
Valla is countered by
As a frail Ranged Assassin, Valla tends to naturally struggle against other
high-damage Assassins who have the ability
to effectively gap close past her
Vault's range or otherwise sneak up on her
(such has Zeratul). With little in the way of
self-peeling, make sure to stay near your Healer when possible
against such Heroes, and make no bold attempts at outplaying your opponents.

guide.title: Valla's Maps
guide.text:
Valla's stronger maps
Valla's average maps
Valla's weaker maps
None
As a well-rounded Ranged Assassin, Valla is not particularly
weak on any Maps. In general, it is better for her to remain accompanied
while laning due to her relative frailty, something that
should not be an issue for most Maps. Since she is good in long teamfights, she is
excellent in maps that feature those, like Infernal Shrines, or Volskaya Foundry.
A special mention should be made for Battlefield of Eternity,
where her Hungering Arrow build really shines.

guide.title: Valla's Tips and Tricks
guide.text:
Hatred empowers Valla's Basic Attacks and increases her Movement Speed; try and attack something at least once every 5 seconds so that your stacks do not fall off.
Hungering Arrow has a high Mana cost and will home unto undesirable targets, such as Minions and Summons; avoid using the Ability unless it is going to deal useful damage.
Multishot is your main waveclearing tool. Its wide area of effect also makes it excellent for checking hidden areas, revealing Stealthed Heroes, and dismounting opponents.
Vault can be used offensively, as a gap-closer, and defensively, to create space between yourself and opponents and dodge Abilities. Limit your offensive use of the Ability, as it leaves you vulnerable.
Strafe's reliability goes up as opponents use up their crowd control Abilities; keep track of their Cooldowns, and remain on the move so as to minimise the chance you will be interrupted.
Rain of Vengeance is better used as a follow-up or as a self-peeling tool than merely for dealing damage.
With Fire At Will, in teamfights Gloom can be always used before using Multishot, as it will instantly restack most of the consumed Hatred.
See our Abilities page for further information »

guide.title: Valla's Role in the Current Meta
guide.text:
Valla's outstanding single-target sustain damage allows her to put an
extreme amount of pressure on anything within her Basic Attack range.
Her on-demand area of effect damage and poke allow her to reliably deal damage
in all situations. A high baseline Movement Speed,
Vault, and Frost Shot
grant her respectable options for self-peeling, though they do not
help her against crowd control.
Valla is extremely strong against Healer-heavy
metas, as such Heroes do not
typically have the tools to force her to play defensively to reduce her
effectiveness. Picking her early during drafts may incite opposing
players to choose dive-oriented Heroes, which must rely on playing
aggressively and on very good coordination to succeed against her. Picking her
later in a draft may leave her completely uncountered and able to freely
deal her damage.

Hungering Arrow has a high Mana cost and will home unto undesirable targets, such as Minions and Summons; avoid using the Ability unless it is going to deal useful damage.

abilities.title: Hungering Arrow
abilities.text:
Hungering Arrow
(Q)
Valla
Mana: 60
Cooldown: 10 seconds
Fire an arrow that deals 140 (+4% per level) damage to the first target hit, then seeks up to 2 additional enemies, prioritizing Heroes, dealing 80 (+4% per level) damage. Can hit an enemy multiple times.
The difficulty with using Hungering Arrow is that it will often home in on
undesirable entities such as Minions, Summons, and Structures, if they stand
between you and your intended target. The only reliable way of ensuring that
Hungering Arrow will hit a specific enemy is to simply position yourself in
such a way that there is nothing standing between you and your target. This can
be achieved by flanking your target or quickly
clearing nearby Minions, usually with Multishot. Given Hungering Arrow's
long cooldown and extremely strong single-target damage potential—equivalent
to approximately 3 Basic Attacks—it should only be used when you are certain
that the Ability will successfully hit an important target and that its damage
is going to be useful.

abilities.title: Multishot
abilities.text:
Multishot
(W)
Valla
Mana: 75
Cooldown: 13 seconds
Deal 159 damage to enemies within the target area.
Multishot's large area of effect, solid damage, and powerful Talents make
it a key Ability. It is typically used on-Cooldown during laning, both as a
waveclearing and harassment tool, and during team fights, simply as a
way of outputting significant area of effect damage. Try to hit as many
enemies as possible with Multishot so as to maximise its efficiency. The
Ability's long range and large area of effect also make it an excellent tool for dismounting and
revealing Stealthed Heroes. The Frost Shot Talent turns
Multishot into one of the most powerful and reliable movement reducing effect in
the game, allowing you to kite and hinder escape attempts
like no other Hero can.

abilities.title: Vault
abilities.text:
Vault
(E)
Valla
Mana: 50
Cooldown: 10 seconds
Dash to the target area. Valla's next Basic Attack within 2 seconds deals 6% increased damage per stack of Hatred.
Vault is extremely versatile; it complements Valla's kit perfectly by
allowing her to quickly reposition to improve the accuracy of her Abilities
and Basic Attack uptime. It can also be used defensively to create breathing
room between herself and dangerous melee attackers, such as Greymane, Thrall,
Sonya, or Zeratul, or to quickly avoid dangerous Abilities, such as
Apocalypse, Hinterland Blast,
Primal Grasp, or Hook.
Avoid using Vault's cooldown offensively, as keen opponents will be quick to
capitalise on this long window of vulnerability unless it helps you safely
secure a kill. Remember that Vault improves your next Basic Attack's damage by
a significant amount, which may make the difference between getting a kill or
not.

abilities.title: Strafe
abilities.text:
In this section we discuss how this Heroic Ability works and give some tips on how to use it.
If you are looking for a detailed explanation on when and why you should pick it,
check out the dedicated section in the Talent Build page.
Strafe
(R)
Valla
Heroic
Mana: 60
Cooldown: 60 seconds
Rapidly attack enemies within 10 range for 70 (+4% per level) damage per hit, prioritizing Heroes over Minions. Valla is able to move and use Vault while strafing. Lasts for 4 seconds.
Strafe is very powerful in terms of raw damage output, and has a relatively
short cooldown when compared to other Heroic Abilities. Left uninterrupted, it
can be a deciding factor in team fights, able to damage frail Heroes for nearly
half of their total Health pool. This power comes at a cost: Strafe's
relatively short range means that you must position yourself aggressively, at
times jeopardising your own safety. Successful Strafe usage also hinges upon
predicting, keeping track of, and avoiding reliable interrupts, such
as Polymorph, Shadow Charge,
and Hammer of Justice,
which can completely neutralise the Ability.

abilities.title: Rain of Vengeance
abilities.text:
In this section we discuss how this Heroic Ability works and give some tips on how to use it.
If you are looking for a detailed explanation on when and why you should pick it,
check out the dedicated section in the Talent Build page.
Rain of Vengeance
(R)
Valla
Heroic
Mana: 50
Charges: 2
Recharge Time: 50 seconds
Launch a wave of Shadow Beasts that deals 250 (+4% per level) damage and Stuns enemies in the target area for 0.5 seconds.
Stores up to 2 charges.
Rain of Vengeance's power stems from its near-instantaneousness and combo
potential. Following up strong
area of effect crowd control Abilities
can often secure kills or ease the
application of other combo pieces. As a defensive tool, Rain of Vengeance can be
used to Stun nearby Heroes in order to create some breathing room and deter them
from approaching you, or to interrupt channeled Abilities.
It should be noted that the shockwave-like aspect of the Ability means that enemies that are standing closer
to Valla will be Stunned and damaged earlier than those standing further away.
Vault can be used offensively as a gap-closer to get as close to your intended
target as possible in order to prevent them from avoiding the Ability's effects.

abilities.title: Hatred
abilities.text:
Hatred
(D)
Valla
Passive
Basic Attacks grant a stack of Hatred, up to 10. Each Hatred stack increases Basic Attack damage by 8% and Movement Speed by 1%. Lasts 5 seconds.
Hatred is what allows Valla to be one of the highest sustain
single-target damage dealing ranged Heroes. While being able to constantly
deliver Basic Attacks is key to playing any Ranged Assassin, it is
especially important to Valla given Hatred's stacking nature. Her fast baseline
Attack Speed somewhat helps with this, however, stutter-stepping truly is the key to
making the most out of Hatred, and Valla as a whole.

talent_pages.title: Discussion
talent_pages.text:
Puncturing Arrow is an interesting choice for single-target
burst builds. It is excellent when combined with other
Hungering Arrow Talents.
It can be a good choice on Battlefield of Eternity,
as a Hungering Arrow Build can quickly
defeat Immortals due to Monster Hunter's extra
PvE damage.
Fire At Will not only increases your Multishot
damage, but also makes it much easier for Valla to stack Hatred. This is an
excellent benefit against aggressive enemy compositions that will be focusing you.
Since this is an unending Quest, it is important to try to maximize your
stacks during the early to mid game, as it will make a great difference at the end of the
game.
Creed of the Hunter is an excellent Talent for a Basic Attack Build.
The 20% extra Attack Speed from the Loan will not only increase
your DPS, but will also make it much easier to stack the quest. However, it is important
to be extremely cautious, as each death will come with big drawbacks.

talent_pages.title: Discussion
talent_pages.text:
Arsenal improves Valla's damage, safety, and Mana control
during fights. With this Talent, Fire At Will
will trigger much more often in teamfights, consequently increasing the rate
in which Valla obtains Hatred and quest stacks.
Death Dealer provides a meaningful burst
damage, as long as you have several Hatred stacks. It can
be used to execute low-Health Minions to provide another vault, that can be used to
escape or to kill an enemy. The cooldown reduction greatly reduces the window in which
you are vulnerable in teamfights, being a great pick against
skillshot-reliant compositions. However, we only recommend this
Talent in a Basic Attacks Build.
Repeating Arrow is excellent in
a Hungering Arrow Build. The extra
Arrow provided by it will significantly increase your burst potential.
This Talent has outstanding synergy with Acrobat
at Level 20.

talent_pages.title: Discussion
talent_pages.text:
Although Monster Hunter makes no difference in teamfights, it makes Valla one of the
most efficient Mercenary Camp killer in the game, especially when combined with
the Repeating Arrow Talent. Monster Hunter is particularly effective on
Battlefield of Eternity, where it can be used to take down the Immortal with ease.
Frost Shot is an excellent and versatile Talent. It is
a great choice in a Hungering Arrow Build,
but can also be useful in a Multishot Build too.
The other options are excellent in their specific niches, and this Talent
should only be picked if you do not need the extra Movement Speed from
Hot Pursuit or the PvE damage
from Monster Hunter.
Hot Pursuit's Movement Speed increase allows you to
keep up with (or kite)
most targets with ease, greatly improving your Basic Attack uptime.
Overall, the extra movespeed will be useful in every game, and will be even better if you can
get several of Hatred stacks from Fire At Will
at the start of a fight.

talent_pages.title: Discussion
talent_pages.text:
In this section we discuss when and why to pick a given Heroic Ability.
If you want to read how they work in detail and/or you are looking for some tips on how to use them,
check them out on the Abilities and Strategy page.
As Strafe and Rain of Vengeance
are both situationally powerful, the choice of one or the other is based on
personal preference and team compositions.
Strafe has the potential of dealing more damage over a larger area than
Rain of Vengeance. However, its channeled nature and long duration make it prone
to being interrupted, unlike Rain of Vengeance, which is instantaneous.
Rain of Vengeance also provides you with a reliable Stun to protect yourself and
your allies, to interrupt other
channeled Abilites, or to keep enemy Heroes in place for longer
while they get focused down by your team.

talent_pages.title: Discussion
talent_pages.text:
Siphoning Arrows provides less survivability than its counterparts, but
does so in a burst fashion with Abilities, being useful if the opposing team can easily blind
or punish Valla when she tries to deliver Basic attacks. It is excellent with
Repeating Arrow and Acrobat. However, this Talent
does not add any protection against burst damage. Against enemies
that can easily kill you in a combo, it might be better to pick Gloom
instead, as it will greatly increase your effective Health at those moments.
Tempered by Discipline is a great Talent if you can easily deliver
Basic Attacks in fights, being a great addition in games against a tough
frontline, as Valla will be able to damage them constantly,
while also sustaining herself. Still, like Siphoning Arrows, this
Talent does not add any protection to burst damage, which is one of
Valla's main weaknesses, so pick it cautiously.
Gloom provides a huge amount of permanent survivability, on top of
having an outstanding activated effect that will let you survive any
Ability-based burst. Remember that although powerful, the activated effect of this Talent
reduces your overall damage. This Talent is particularly powerful with Fire At Will
at Level 1, because you can quickly reacquire the Hatred stacks
lost by using it.

talent_pages.title: Level 16 Talents for Valla
talent_pages.text:

(Level 16)

While at max Hatred, Multishot's cooldown recharges 50% faster.
Passive: Reduce Multishot's Mana cost from 75 to 55.

(Level 16)

While at max Hatred, increase all damage dealt by 10%.

(Level 16)
Valla
Every 3rd Basic Attack against the same Hero deals an additional 4% of their maximum Health as damage.

talent_pages.title: Discussion
talent_pages.text:
Punishment is not as effective as it sounds. In perfect conditions,
it will reduce Multishot's cooldown from 13 seconds to 8.7 seconds, which
cannot compare to Manticore's extra damage. However, Punishment can be
a good choice in games where Valla cannot consistently deliver several Basic Attacks in a
row (like against several blinds, or extremely high burst damage).
Seething Hatred slightly increases all damage dealt by Valla.
Mostly, this Talent will be overshadowed by Manticore, but it can
be useful with Repeating Arrow and Acrobat,
because most of the damage will come from Hungering Arrow, instead of
from Basic Attacks.
Manticore is an excellent choice in most games, as it adds
between 16% (attacking Hanzo) to 32% (attacking Blaze) extra damage to your Basic Attacks.
Just be sure to focus your attacks against your intended target.
Manticore has notable synergy with Creed of the Hunter and
Farflight Quiver.

talent_pages.title: Discussion
talent_pages.text:
Death Siphon is an excellent Talent, it enhances everything
in Strafe, turning it into a teamfight-deciding Heroic.
If enemies do not cancel it with a Stun
or Silence, you will probably win the
fight due to how oppressive it is. After getting this Talent,
it is important to maintain 2 targets in your range during Strafe,
as it is necessary for the duration to not reduce quickly.
Storm of Vengeance signficantly increases your single-target damage output,
but does little to keep you safe as Farflight Quiver or
Acrobat would.
This Talent is useful while under a limited amount of pressure, and synergises
particularly well with Manticore to obliterate Healthier Heroes.
Acrobat is an excellent Talent when combined with
Repeating Arrow. It enables 4 consecutives casts of
Hungering Arrow, dealing enough damage to burst
down a healthy Tank or multiple squishy Heroes.
Farflight Quiver significantly improves the reliability of your Basic Attacks while
simultaneously keeping you at a safer distance. The range also indirectly
improves your Hatred generation as it makes Basic Attacks easier to
deliver safely. At 10 Hatred stacks Valla can attack Keeps, Towers or Core from outside
its ranges.
